title: Never take over a live user host lock, and release only a run's own
summary: A lock held by a live run for more than 10 minutes is no longer taken over: when `ia host claude --user` finds its lock, `<IA home>/claude/.lock`, held by another run whose pid is still running, @inventarch/distribution now refuses IA-DIST-INSTALL-BUSY however old the lock is, since its age does not show that its owner stopped. A lock whose pid has died is still taken over at any age, and one whose pid is empty or unparseable after 10 seconds; a lock holding 0, a negative number or a number above 2147483647 is now judged the same way, where it used to wait out the 10 minutes. A stale lock whose pid another process has since reused now stays busy until it is removed by hand, as the unchanged IA-DIST-INSTALL-BUSY message says to do when no run is active. A run now writes its pid, a space and a random token, and at its end removes the lock only while it is still a regular file holding exactly that text and its name still names that file, so a run whose lock was replaced no longer removes the replacement and lets another run acquire the lock while the replacement's owner is active. A lock in the earlier format, a pid alone, is still judged by its pid, and a run's release leaves it in place. Earlier releases running at the same time still take over a lock older than 10 minutes. A brief window between the release's check and its removal remains, as Node has no unlink-if-same.
